h: Carriages, Cycle Trails and a Cliff Railway
p: The zoo's spot in the hills above Barnstaple puts it on the edge of a part of Devon that's packed with family days out, from National Trust estates to heritage railways.

Arlington Court, a National Trust house just a few miles away, has a famous collection of horse-drawn carriages in its stables, plus woodland walks, a lake and gardens. It's a nice gentle pairing with the zoo, especially for grandparents. Back in Barnstaple, the Pannier Market is a grand Victorian covered market that's still busy with stalls selling food, crafts and odds and ends, and Butchers Row next door is a quirky little street of shops.

Barnstaple is also a starting point for the Tarka Trail, a flat, traffic-free path following the old railway line along the Taw estuary towards Instow and Bideford. You can hire bikes in town, and it's perfect for families with young riders. The trail takes its name from Tarka the Otter, the novel set in this part of Devon.
For a day on the moor's northern coast, head up to Lynton and Lynmouth. The water-powered cliff railway linking the two villages has been running since 1890 and is a ride everyone should try once.

At the zoo, it's worth asking about the seasonal animal experiences, and checking the talk times as soon as you arrive so you can plan your route around them. Because the zoo is open year round, it's a handy option for an out-of-season break too.
